name: Baked Potato

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Fluffy and delicious, if only you had some butter.

description:
The baked potato is a power level 1 food item that provides 20 sustenance and 20 health when eaten. They can be cooked at either a campfire or grill.

(Journal)
The simplicity. The elegance. Few things in life are quite as dependable as a good old Baked Potato. Crispy exterior, fluffy interior, and it goes well with just about anything.

name: Beef & Tomato Stew

infobox.label: Recipe (Stone Range)

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)

description:
Beef & tomato stew is a consumable food item that provides 60 health and 65 sustenance. It is made with grilled tomatoes, steak, and dried redberries in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

(Journal)
Tomatoes go well with just about everything. They enhance the flavours of anything they’re paired with and a nice beef stew is no exception. The combined flavours are comforting as well as filling, and almost make you forget that you’re a long way from home, on a continent filled with murderous dragons.

name: Beltfish Broth

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A potent soup made from beltfish.

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)
infobox.value: 1 × Steamed Beltfish + 1 × Peach + 1 × Fried Cabbage → 1 × Beltfish Broth (Cooking 20 XP)

description:
Beltfish broth is a consumable food item that provide 130 health and 25 sustenance. It is made with steamed beltfish, peach, and fried cabbage and despite being a filling meal, can only be cooked in a cooking range.

(Journal)
The Moon Garou don't like to waste a kill. Every last organ and morsel of flesh is eaten or used in some capacity, in honour of the creature that surrendered its life.

In that spirit, beltfish broth is the final stop for a beltfish's innards. Eyeballs, teeth, fins, organs and even the odd parasite ("tapeworm, tapeworm, you make my belly squirm", as the garou song goes) are boiled and served in this delightful dish.

name: Berry Compote

infobox.label: Status
infobox.value: Removed from the game (as of Eye on Ashenfall - 0.9.1)

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A fruity medley of cooked berries. A great, sweet treat for enjoying in the wild.

description:
Berry compote is a consumable food item that can be crafted by combining redberries and dwellberries at a cooking pot. When consumed it provides moderate sustenance and 5 lifeward. There is also a 5% chance to produce a rat roast whilst making a berry compote.

(Journal)
Berries and more berries, what could be better? A sweet and sour sensation in each mouthful. A refreshing, yet enjoyable meal. Well, more like a dessert, but no one’s judging you.

name: Berry Drizzle Pan-Seared

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Made by combining smoked herring, seared anchovies and dried dwellberry.

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)
infobox.value: 1 × Smoked Herring + 1 × Seared Anchovies + 1 × Dried Dwellberries → 1 × Berry Drizzle Pan-Seared (Cooking 20 XP)

description:
Berry drizzle pan-seared is a consumable food item that provides 160 health and 65 sustenance. It is made with smoked herring, seared anchovies, and dried dwellberries in a cooking range.

(Journal)
"Pan-seared what?", you may ask. Well, pan-seared herring and anchovies, my good fellow. That might sound like a lot of fish in one meal, but some dwellberry acts as a sweet binding agent, making the whole eating-process rather delightful. It's a meal that's been around for generations, and you will often hear battle-worn adventurers wishing that they were back home for 'some of mammy's pan-seared'.

We suspect that the berry drizzle pan-seared that you've made is NOT from mammy, however. We may be wrong: it's very possible that there's a quest that we've forgotten.

name: Braised Catfish

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: If your feline hungry, eat a catfish. Grants the Sea Life perk.[sic]

infobox.label: Recipe (Campfire)
infobox.value: 1 × Raw Armoured Catfish → 1 × Braised Catfish (Cooking 10 XP)

infobox.label: Recipe (Grill)
infobox.value: 1 × Raw Armoured Catfish → 1 × Braised Catfish (Cooking 10 XP)

description:
Braised catfish is a consumable food item that provides 120 health and 30 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw armoured catfish on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in stuffed catfish.

(Journal)
Cooking a braised catfish is no mean feat. The process involves removing the armoured shell while managing to avoid the nerve-endings that, once severed, can release a poison that is fatal to humans. Then a chef needs to achieve precisely the right temperature to neutralise the latent poison without - again - activating it.

Of course, if you want fewer friends, braised catfish is easy as pie to cook.

name: Braised Undead Eel

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Makes you queasy but does wonders for hunger. Grants the Warding Fish perk.[sic]

infobox.label: Recipe (Campfire)
infobox.value: 1 × Raw Undead Eel → 1 × Braised Undead Eel (Cooking 10 XP)

infobox.label: Recipe (Grill)
infobox.value: 1 × Raw Undead Eel → 1 × Braised Undead Eel (Cooking 10 XP)

description:
Braised undead eel is a consumable food item that provides 60 health and 25 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw undead eel on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in fish fry.

(Journal)
Sweet Saradomin on High, why on earth are you braising an undead eel? Are you a mind rune short of a rune pouch?

Perhaps it's a dare, and you're going to get a hefty payout after making it? I can't think of any other reason, sane or otherwise, why you would fish for the horrible, wriggly thing, pick it up afterwards, then braise it, which - we may add - is a process to DRAW OUT FLAVOURS.

What next? Bury it in the ground for days and eat it afterwards? I would not put it past you.

name: Bread

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Crusty brown outside, pillowy white inside.

description:
Bread is a power level 2 food. It can be created by using a bag of flour on a kiln. It heals 20 health and provides 30 sustenance when consumed.

(Journal)
Simple wheat, water, yeast and salt, combined together and incinerated within an oven. A staple across many cultures and species across Gielinor and beyond. The Icyene of Hallow enjoy a flatbread that they can wrap food in, for a meal on the wind. The aviansie of Abbinah, when the limited wheat is available, prefer a thick and sturdy bread, so that each bite lasts longer. Elves enjoy a sourdough, priding themselves on how long they can keep the starter alive.

For the people of Ashenfall, much like their cousins in the mainland, a simple loaf is more than enough.

infobox.value: Can be eaten raw, but wouldn't recommend it. Can be cooked alone or as an ingredient in cooking meals.

description:
Cadavaberries are a consumable food item that provides 10 sustenance but also 20 Soulscourge, which will cause damage over time if it builds to 100. They are also a power level 4 ingredient, which means they can be cooked at a campfire or grill into dried cadavaberries starting at Cooking Level 41, and not burnt into burnt cadavaberries at level 50. They can be collected from cadavaberry bushes in Fellhollow and Farmed from cadavaberry bush (Farming) grown from cadavaberry seeds.

(Journal)
Don’t eat them. No, seriously, don’t. At least not raw. Cadavaberries are poisonous and deadly, often used in sinister ceremonies of ritual sacrifice. The cadavaberries on Ashenfall are equally toxic, but can be coaxed into good behaviour with the judicious addition of fire.

The toxins can be burned away, providing a surprisingly pleasant tasting berry beneath. But, one must be careful, for preparing them wrong is the last mistake someone is likely to make.

It can be cooked from undead meat at either a campfire or a grill, and is used in dubious meat pie.

(Journal)
Despite the appearance of their former owners and the deeply unpleasant smell emanating from it, undead meat is not rotten. It, like the nature of its former owners, is preserved in a state between life and death, as if it's on the cusp of souring, but never quite getting there.

This unique nature gives it some very interesting properties, but sadly, flavour isn't one of them.

(Journal)
The grease. The sizzling scents. The feeling of your arteries withering just from a single glance at the dish. Is there anything in life as close to the divine as a nice, cheeky fry up?

Popular among those who have consumed a few too many gnomish cocktails the night before, a cheeky fry up is hailed as a great cure for the pounding headache that follows such indulgences.

They can also be used to make dwellberry infusion, feathered lure, as well as some potions, a decoration, and weapons. They can be collected from dwellberry bushes in Fractured Plains and Stormtouched Highlands, Farmed from dwellberries (Farming) grown from dwellberry seeds, and found in chests in Ghornfell.

Pretty blue berries, go well in a cheesecake.

Do you know what they call an eggs royale in Asgarnia? 'Salmon and egg'. Barbarians.

There aren't many flavours that go together as well as salmon and egg. Pork and cheese. Bread and butter. Fishing potions and a hangover.

(Journal)
A 'fish fry' is something of a misnomer as only the eel is a fish, and even that's questionable now that it's undead. The lobster is most definitely a crustacean, and a cabbage is a holy orb of sustenance, delivered by the majestic Brassica Prime. Therefore, not a fish.

We give a fish fry a pass, mainly because it's a Fellhollow delicacy, once favoured by Ravanna. It was invented after a sailor saw a lobster and eel fighting and threw a well-aimed cabbage. He fried the result and lo, fish fry was born.

Thick and juicy, the Flank Steak is more filling than you might first expect. The dense meat means each mouthful makes you fuller for longer.

Although, the mushrooms are a little much: they could probably have been thinned out. Maybe removed? Yes, remove them. The bread, too. Is it needed? Would you perhaps consider removing the envelope of bread that houses the sweet cabbage missive? Your dribbly jowls will thank us.

While the first few attempts resulted in terrible food poisoning — Guthix was a god, not a chef — the perfected recipe soon became a favourite once he mixed in mushrooms. This was because the mushrooms absorbed much of the toxins, making it much more palatable.

Meat and mushrooms, an alliance that stretches back across time. Both flavours mixing together to create a unified taste explosion. On Ashenfall, the mushrooms are infused with anima and draw toxins away from those who ingest them. Popular with anyone looking to avoid poisoning.

Fried cabbage is a power level 1 food item that can be cooked at either a campfire or grill. Fried cabbages have 20 sustenance and 20 health when consumed.

(Journal)
Brassica Prime – the god of cabbages – gifted the world with this delicious vegetable, to lead the faithful on the noble path of nutrition. In his infinite, leafy, wisdom, he taught the early settlers about how one might fry the leaves so that they would be even more delicious.

Now Fried Cabbages offer those who consume it the strength and stamina needed to brave the hardships of Ashenfall.

name: Fried Egg
description:
Fried eggs are a power level 1 food item made by cooking an egg at a campfire or grill. Fried eggs have 20 sustenance and 20 health when consumed.

(Journal)
Slimy, greasy and everything you need. There are few things as surprisingly satisfying as a fried egg sandwich. If only you had some bread!

Contrary to popular humour the aviansie have no issue with people eating eggs around them. Indeed many of them have raptor like tastes and will happily consume the eggs of livestock birds. Boiled almhas (a domesticated bat-like creature) eggs were popular snacks on Abbinah, yet those eggs could not be fried as they would combust dramatically when exposed to a naked flame.

Fortunately chicken eggs are far less flammable.

Although the preparation leaves you weeping, and the smell makes it worse, fried onions are a delicious meal to get you through a difficult day.

Fried salmon may not be the most substantial or healing of fish, but it's celebrated for its moist texture and delicious taste.

Famously, it was the subject of a smear campaign from the Saradominist church to get it banned as a foodstuff, as they objected to the populace describing it as 'moist'. They deemed the adjective 'unsaintly'.

(Journal)
A fried sardine, also known as a charred pilchard or 'pilcharred', is the go-to snack for a fisherman's pocket. If you see a stoic fisherman who talks very little, it's likely because they've got a mouthful of fried sardine and don't want to reveal the bones between their teeth.

Fried sardines were also the subject of a failed business venture by a dwarf called Drorkar. He tried to manufacture 'tins' that would contain these sardines, with smithed 'rings' to open their tiny metal coffins. It was roundly rejected and cost the dwarf a great deal.

Grannies everywhere are masters of this dish. Delicious fruits, a touch of sugar, some delightful pastry and that final ingredient - a dark blessing to ancient gods.

Or love, that works too.

With the pact complete, these pies allow you those fond memories of comfort, hope and family. Something much needed out in the wilds of Ashenfall.

A great meal for a real fun guy… sorry.

Popular with terrible pun writers and villagers alike, roasted mushrooms were a staple diet across much of Ashenfall. Wild Knights would forage for the best mushrooms to enjoy on their long hunts.

The fortifying effect of mushrooms made them even more popular with those braving poison-filled Bloodblight Swamp.

Until recently, grilled trout was prescribed by doctors thanks to its regenerative properties. 'A grilled trout a day will keep the gout away' was the common phrase. After a study by the Cook's Guild in far-off Varrock, however, it was found that regular eaters of grilled trout were 20% more likely to contract gout.

Don't let that stop you enjoying the bitter notes of a trout. The Cook's Guild did a study and found that 75% of gout-inflicted people thought it was totally worth it.

Only moderately less disgusting than braising an undead eel is grilling an undead bass. At least you can close your eyes and imagine what the bass once was: a tasty fish that took a wrong turn at Ardougne and ended up in the Withering.

At some point in the future, some forward-thinking chef will determine that grilled undead bass is a delicacy. Right now, however, we look at you with the stinkiest of eyes and think 'for shame'.

We are yet to find something that maple syrup does not elevate. Pancakes and bacon are the obvious ones, but try it out on things that are more left-field. Rat meat? Elevated. Terrorbird meat? Elevated. Undead eel? Eelevated.

So, thank you, humble maple tree. You are a true wonder of the culinary and apothecary world. It won't stop us woodcutting you, but know that each cut comes with a maple syrup-sized dollop of guilt.

It is their belief that when there are so few fruits and treasures in the desert, why would someone possibly deny themselves a moment of enjoyment?

name: Raw Monkfish

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Your mouth waters just looking at it.

description:
Raw monkfish is a power level 7 food that can be captured at net fishing spots in the Umbral Sands region. Monkfish are so-called on Ashenfall due to the goddess Elidinis. The Moon Garou, having never seen a monk, adopted the name after the goddess herself named them. "The Moon Garou don't recognise the term 'monk'."... "Which raises the question of why the Moon Garou call these fish 'monkfish' at all. Well, the answer is a little on the boring, perhaps even obvious side. The River Goddess, who many Moon Garou worship, came to Ashenfall from mainland Gielinor, where the monkfish are more prevalent. So she pointed at the fish, said its name, and Bob's your monkfish." (from the Monkfish Fillets journal)

(Journal — Fish)
There are, in fact, two variants of the monkfish. One is the Piscatoris monkfish, known for its gamey taste and slightly depressed countenance. The other is the Ashenfall monkfish, which has a more trout-like flavour and a happier, almost smirking countenance. Anglers, who like to simplify things, distinguish them by calling them 'sad boy' and 'happy boy'.

Both monkfish are 'sad boys' when they're caught, of course.

(Journal — Raw)
It may be called the 'Ashenfall' monkfish, but you'd be hard-pressed to find it anywhere other than in Umbral Sands. That's mostly down to a lack of trade. The Moon Garou are an isolationist sort, preferring to keep their trading partners to other Moon Garou. Their closest non-garou partners would be the Black Knights but they, too, like to keep to themselves, and would prefer to deal with other humans over the garou.

Which is a shame, really, as monkfish deserves to go continental. Ashenfall monkfish is like trout, but with a slight fizzing sensation, similar to popping candy. If you've got a child or garou cub who won't eat their fish, then try them on Ashenfall monkfish. In our house, it's a gateway fish, leading onto other, less gimmicky fish.

They are also a Power Level 1 ingredient, which means they can be cooked at a campfire or grill into dried redberries starting at Cooking level 1, and not burnt into burnt redberries at level 12. They can also be used to make redberry infusion, as well as some potions and decorations. They can be collected from redberry bushes in Temple Woods and Bramblemead Valley, Farmed from redberries (Farming) grown from redberry seeds, and found in chests in Ghornfell.

(Journal)
Eaten at the right time, these simple berries might mean the difference between life and death. A favourite treat for the villagers of Bramblemead, who would mix the berries into various desserts to enjoy. Red berry pie was particularly popular with visiting Wild Knights.

Imagine it. You gather around the table, the warm smell of a freshly cooked roast wafts across the room. Your mother places a bowl of roast potatoes, so divinely crisp that you wonder if they’re even real. Your sibling places a tray of freshly cooked vegetables, a kaleidoscope of colourful foods waiting to be consumed. Your father, doggedly sticking to traditional gender roles as if the past is an anchor weighing him down, slices into the roast serving each of you juicy cuts of meat that make your mouth water.

And what are you doing in all of this? Hrmm? Nothing, that’s what! Pull your life together Stanley!

If your name is not Stanley, you can ignore that above message.

Here on Ashenfall you do not have those smiling faces to reflect upon, only the memories elucidated by the roast meat before you. As you tuck in, you’ll recall those moments of happier times, before you got stranded here with nothing.

Smoked herring is not, as the idiom will claim, 'red'. It is more of an orange, coppery colour. That means the term 'red herring' is something of a red herring. Which tracks.

The process of smoking a herring has changed over the years. In the Second Age, a herring would be smoked in the village elder's pipe, in the hope that some of the elder's wisdom would transfer to the fish. In the Third Age, entrepreneurial Zamorakians would line their demon portals with herring in the hope of an infernal aftertaste. Nowadays, people use a cooking pot.

(Journal)
One of the most challenging dishes to prepare on Ashenfall is the smoked infernal eel. The whole process is an olfactory gauntlet. You are bombarded with such a succession of smells, some wonderful, some horrifying, that it can feel like sprinting through the back alleys of Varrock. Some chefs from the Cook's Guild have compared it to 'seeing one's life flash before their eyes'. Except with noses.

Complete the gauntlet, however, and the bounty is worth it. Many people call smoked infernal eel a 'delicacy' but the term doesn't really suit. Delicacy is derived from 'delicate', after all. The taste is more like a salt-chinchompa exploding under your tongue.

name: Squeaking Sausage

description:
Squeaking sausage is a consumable food item that provides +0.5 Resist Shocked Buildup, 80 health, and 80 sustenance as well as the perk Grounded, which grants resistance to shock effects for 300 seconds. It is made with dried dwellberries, fried onions, and rat roast in a cooking range.

(Journal)
Sausages are proof that ignorance is bliss. When you bite into the juicy banger, you are best served not to think about its contents. Nor about the origins of the skin that contains the meat so well.

Although simple, and lacking in much needed herbs and spices, these sausages manage to curb your hunger well enough to help you avoid thinking too much about what they’re made from.

Ignore the squeak… and the whiskers.

name: Steak

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A delicious steak. The perfect campfire meal.

description:
Steak a consumable food item that provide 20 sustenance and 30 health when eaten. They can be cooked at either a campfire or grill.

(Journal)
Sizzling on the grill, there is little that has united middle-aged villagers more than a steak seared to perfection. Brynmoor villagers would gather around grills to discuss hunting, village politics and anything else that came to mind, all as an excuse to silently judge the way the current chef prepared this simple meal.

name: Steak 'N' Eggs

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A marvelous way, to start your day.

infobox.label: Recipe (Stone Range)

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)

description:
Steak 'n' eggs is a consumable food item that provides 40 health and 50 sustenance. It is made with fried egg and steak in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

(Journal)
Some meals require silence. As you chew each mouthful, you reminisce on times past. On loved ones lost. On friends remembered. On moments that bring a smile to your face – simple and uncomplicated, without the weight of the world’s burdens crushing down on you. This is one of those meals.

(Journal)
Steak, if you ask me, is infinitely diminished by putting it between two slices of bread. Steak should stand proud on its own, garnished with salt and barely introduced to a flame.

As a journal-writer I can't stop you. My powers are limited to shaming you from the dark recesses of your interfaces.

name: Steamed Beltfish

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A long, tough meal. Don't eat it in one swallow.

description:
Steamed beltfish is a consumable food item that provides 100 health and 30 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw beltfish on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in beltfish broth and swabbie pie.

(Journal)
The custom with a steamed beltfish is to eat it all in one, like a sword-eater swallowing their blade whole. The Moon Garou chomp it down like they were raised by pythons. The human gullet isn't quite built for this method of eating, so be careful if you're invited over for a Moon Garou celebration. Aim for the smaller ones at the banquet table. Chew subtly.

name: Stir-Fry

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Made by combining dried giant krill, dried redberry[sic] and smoked infernal eel.

infobox.label: Perk 1

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)

description:
Stir-fry is a consumable food item that provides 150 health and 70 sustenance as well as the perks Sea Legs and Sea Life, which makes players immune to the slowing effects of water and restores 3 health every second for 600 seconds. It is made with dried giant krill, dried dwellberries, and smoked infernal eel in a cooking range.

(Journal)
Imagine if we named all our meals after the processes that make it. Ooh, I'm going to make a pot of boil-strain-pour. I might follow it up with a batch of roll-cut-bakes. It's all a bit odd, if you ask me.

The Ashenfall stir-fry is something of a curio when compared to the mainland's. To make a mainland version, you would have to swap the krill for seaweed and the infernal eel for lava eel. Whisper it, though: I think the Ashenfall version is better. And it goes particularly well with some grow-chop-fries.

name: Stuffed Catfish

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Made by combining dried giant krill, fried cabbage and a braised catfish.

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)
infobox.value: 1 × Dried Giant Krill + 1 × Fried Cabbage + 1 × Braised Catfish → 1 × Stuffed Catfish (Cooking 20 XP)

description:
Stuffed catfish is a consumable food item that provides 200 health and 80 sustenance. It is made with dried giant krill, fried cabbage, and braised catfish in a cooking range.

(Journal)
Perhaps it's a good thing that fish have no idea what their future holds. We can only imagine their reactions. "Sorry, chap, you're going to have your armour removed, your innards replaced with cabbage, and krill pushed into your orifices."

Would it soften the blow if they knew how tasty they became? A stuffed catfish is elevated by the brassic flavours, achieving culinary peaks that are unrivalled on Ashenfall. We like to think that the knowledge would soften the blow.

name: Sun Baked Sole

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: Even when cooked it still smells a great deal.

infobox.label: Recipe (Campfire)
infobox.value: 1 × Raw Desert Sole → 1 × Sun Baked Sole (Cooking 10 XP)

infobox.label: Recipe (Grill)
infobox.value: 1 × Raw Desert Sole → 1 × Sun Baked Sole (Cooking 10 XP)

description:
Sun baked sole is a consumable food item that provides 130 health and 30 sustenance. It is made by cooking raw desert sole on either a campfire or a grill, and is used in swabbie pie.

(Journal)
Most Moon Garou would consider an adventurer's version of dune-smoking to be a pale imitation of the true process. 'Real' dune-smoking involves burying a raw desert sole deep within a dune, preferably a couple of metres down. Inside the dune, it alternately cooks and cools with the Scorch and cold nights. The sand helps to delay the rotting process, but - I am slightly debatably told by Moon Garou chefs - that a little bit of rotting never hurt anyone.

name: Swabbie Pie

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A pie reserved for the less prestigious members of a ship's crew.

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)
infobox.value: 1 × Sun Baked Sole + 1 × Steamed Beltfish + 1 × Bread + 1 × Baked Potato → 1 × Swabbie Pie (Cooking 20 XP)

description:
Swabbie pie is a consumable food item that provide 220 health and 80 sustenance. It is made with sun baked sole, steamed beltfish, bread, and baked potato in a cooking range.

(Journal)
The Moon Garou aren't particularly hot on pies. They like their dishes open and aromatic, engulfing all of the senses. A pie is the anti-garou dish: it disguises itself until its pastry is broken, and only then do you get that delicious waft of smells. It's a culinary jack-in-the-box.

Which is a shame, as I think the Moon Garou are really missing a trick. The ripe smell of a desert sole is particularly suited to pies, as it ambushes the eater when they break the seal. That's where the 'swabby' comes in, as eaters will often have to wipe their eyes from the olfactory assault.

name: Sweet Veg Ball

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A marvelous amalgamation of sweet and savoury.

infobox.label: Perk
infobox.value: Knowledgable Nourishment — Grants a 10% XP BOOST

infobox.label: Recipe (Stone Range)

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)
infobox.value: 1 × Fried Cabbage + 1 × Baked Potato + 1 × Dried Redberries → 1 × Sweet Veg Ball (Cooking 20 XP)

Sweet veg ball is a consumable food item that provides 70 health 65 sustenance as well as the perk Knowledgable Nourishment, which increases the player's experience gain in all skills by 10% for 300 seconds. It is made with fried cabbage, baked potato, and dried redberries in a stone range or a cooking range. It is learned by unlocking Amateur Culinaromancer at level 16 Cooking, and requires interacting with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

(Journal)
Popular among gnomes, this sticky ball of fruits and vegetables is a combination of savoury and sweet that almost feels like it shouldn’t work. Yet it does.

There is a crispness to the outer shell, savoury and salty, which gives way to a delicious fruity sweetness beneath.

Gnomish ambassadors would create large numbers of these sweet treats, piled high on silver platters, to delight visiting dignitaries at lavish receptions. Diplomats would often joke about being spoiled by such treats. Which is ironic really, as these spoil very quickly, so enjoy them now while you can.

name: Umbral Kebab

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A garou delicacy, ideal for those night-time munchies.

infobox.label: Perk 1
infobox.value: Frosted Flavours — Grants RESISTANCE to SCORCH buildup

infobox.label: Perk 2
infobox.value: Soul Food — Restore HEALTH over time

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)
infobox.value: 1 × Seared Cactus Steak + 1 × Bread + 1 × Roast Pumpkin + 1 × Steak → 1 × Umbral Kebab (Cooking 20 XP)

description:
Umbral kebab is a consumable food item that provide 80 health and 90 sustenance, as well as the perks Frosted Flavours and Soul Food, which reduces Scorch buildup and restores 8 health every 5 seconds for 300 seconds. It is made with seared cactus steak, bread, roast pumpkin, and steak in a cooking range.

(Journal)
Ah, the humble, versatile kebab. It can be a handy, portable dish, or it can be a sprawling, sloppy one. It can be a snack or a meal; a low-effort munch or a high-end dish that you would serve to in-laws. It can be skewered or open; spicy or mild.

About the only constant is a sense of fulfilment, that you've eaten well and more than enough, alongside a vague, far-off worry that you might be attached to a toilet bowl later on that night.

description:
Undead delight is a consumable food item that provides 180 health and 70 sustenance as well as the perk Sea Life, which restores 3 health every second for 1,200 seconds. It is made with grilled undead bass and grilled tomatoes in a stone range or a cooking range, however a player must interact with a stone range first to learn the recipe.

(Journal)
'Undead Delight' sounds like an audio track from a long-forgotten Halloween event, but NO - it's an unexpectedly tasty meal. The very dead flavours of an undead bass are meshed with the very alive flavours of a tomato, and the combination is capital-D Delicious.

We will admit that it's off-putting that the un-alive also find the Undead Delight tasty. Put it in front of a skeleton, zombie, demon or other wretched being and they will gobble it up like there's no tomorrow.

Crisp and delicious vegetables, neatly fried mushrooms, there are few breakfasts quite as delicious as a fry up, even for those who abjure bacon.

(Journal)
A good soup won’t just fill your stomach, it’ll lift your spirits. Warm and comforting, the taste of home. Popular across all of Gielinor by anyone with a pan and some vegetables.

name: Victoria Sponge Cake

infobox.label: Description
infobox.value: A delicious sponge cake, thankfully without the goblin version of frosting.

infobox.label: Perk
infobox.value: Sugar Rush — REDUCES REST drain by 25%

infobox.label: Recipe (Stone Range)
infobox.value: 2 × Dried Redberries + 2 × Egg + 2 × Redberry Infusion + 4 × Wheat → 1 × Victoria Sponge Cake (Cooking 20 XP)

infobox.label: Recipe (Cooking Range)
infobox.value: 2 × Dried Redberries + 2 × Egg + 2 × Redberry Infusion + 4 × Wheat → 1 × Victoria Sponge Cake (Cooking 20 XP)

description:
Victoria sponge cake is a consumable food item that provides 85 sustenance and 50 health, as well as the perk Sugar Rush, which reduces rest drain by 25% for 300 seconds. It is made with 2 dried redberries, 2 eggs, 2 redberry infusions, and 4 wheat in a stone range or a cooking range after receiving the recipe from the Cook's Assistant quest.

(Journal)
Named after Victoria Thistlethwaite, of Bramblemead, this cake has been popular at the most lavish of parties across the region. Victoria was a well-regarded chef, but one whose culinary obsessions lay only with the sweetest of treats. She would craft biscuits, pastries and candied treats of such quality, that even Bandos once visited her little cafe to try one.

So moved was the god of war by her delicious pastries, that he left three goblins to watch over her as the war against the garou began, and those goblins would defend her with their lives. Unfortunately, goblin lives are surprisingly fleeting at the best of times, and in an actual war they lasted perhaps no more than a few hours. Victoria's little shop was consumed in a terrible inferno, reducing all her sweetest of treats to little more then motes of blackened ash, whisked away in the wind.

In honour of Bandos, and the bond that was struck with this mortal chef, goblins of Ashenfall pass down this cake recipe from generation to generation, in the hope that all might share in the deliciousness.

name: Watermelon Jerky
description:
Watermelon jerky is a power level 4 item that is made by cooking watermelon on a campfire.

(Journal)
Satisfying, if a little chewy.

(Journal)
A delicious pastry crust seals the flavours inside. Warm and filling, each bite designed to fill you with comfort. The flavour is earthy, and rich, letting you shrug off almost anything.
